tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000ms / 30 minutes, max 7200000ms / 2 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

290:- Returning to the usage view after a manual account switch (v158.0): `TryRedirectToUsage`'s post-auth landing whitelist (`/new`, `/chats`, `/chat/`, `/projects`, `/recents`) deliberately excluded the root path, because `/` doubles as the signed-out home page and redirecting it unconditionally loops `/settings/usage → / → /settings/usage`. claude.ai drops a fresh sign-in on `/` about as often as on `/new`, so Switch Account → native "Log out" → sign in as a different user left the panel parked on the home page until the user pressed Refresh. `_sawSignedOutPage` (set whenever the embedded page visits `/login`, `/logout`, `/magic-link` or `/auth`) now promotes `/` to a landing, and `RedirectToUsageIfSettledAsync` requires a non-empty claude.ai `sessionKey` cookie (`HasClaudeSessionCookieAsync`) before navigating — a genuinely signed-out root reads no cookie and is left alone. The flag is cleared as the redirect fires, so a navigate that bounces straight back to `/` cannot re-arm it: one attempt per sign-out. The settle path re-checks `core.Source` both before and after the awaited cookie read, since the await gives the page another chance to move. `/onboarding` is deliberately *not* a landing — an account claude.ai forces through onboarding would ping-pong `/onboarding → /settings/usage` every ~6.5 s (1.5 s settle + 5 s debounce).
292:- Following a Claude CLI account switch (v221.0): the bars come from the WebView2's own claude.ai session, which has nothing to do with the CLI's credentials, so `/logout` + `/login` typed into the terminal (or `claude auth login` anywhere) moved the agent to another account while the bars kept scraping, and refreshing, the old one. Only the ⚙ "Change Account" items signed the page out. `SyncUsageWithClaudeAccountAsync` runs on every background tick (ahead of the foreground-tab guard) and once before the startup refresh. It reads `oauthAccount` from the active side's `~/.claude.json` (the distro's copy for `ClaudeCodeWSL`, with the `wslpath` result cached per session). `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is honored on both sides (`GetClaudeJsonPath`, `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME}` under WSL), because the CLI then keeps the file in that folder and never writes the one in the home directory. It identifies the account as `accountUuid/organizationUuid`, so switching organizations under the same login counts as a switch too, since usage limits are per organization. It falls back to the e-mail address when the UUIDs are missing. No `oauthAccount` (between `/logout` and `/login`) or a half-written file reads as "unknown" and never as a switch. The account the page was last paired with is kept per side (`windows`/`wsl`) in `usage-account.json` next to the settings, not in the settings. Every VS window saves its whole in-memory settings on each scrape, so a second window would write the old account back and then sign the shared page out a second time. The first check on a side only records the account. A window can find the pairing already moved to the account it now reads, because another window handled the switch. It then only drops its own cached snapshot (`_usageAccountSeen`), since its bars would otherwise sit on the old numbers until the next successful scrape. A change calls `SignOutUsageWindowIfActiveAsync(pairedAccount)`, which clears the cached snapshot, signs the page out and shows a main-window info bar (`InfoBarSlot.UsageAccount`) with an "Open Claude Usage" link. It deliberately does not pop the tab, which could steal focus while the user types. The Change Account menu items pass no account, which forgets the pairing, so the CLI login that follows is adopted silently instead of being handled as a second switch.

lines: +- The Claude Usage page no longer signs itself out when it thinks the Claude Code account changed, so a Google sign-in there now sticks. Change Account and the page's own Sign Out / Switch Account still sign it out.
- **Pull from git before the first prompt** is now off by default, and is turned off once for existing installs. If you want it, turn it back on in *⚙ → Settings... → Automation*.
- Multi-line prompts sent to Claude Code through the Command Prompt terminal no longer show stray `[200~` and `[201~` text on Windows 11 24H2 and later.

- Fable gated on usage credits (v215.0): Fable needs usage credits, so `extract()` also reads the balance from the header of `#extra-usage-credits-section` (`[data-settings-group-header]` → last child, e.g. `R$0`) into `UsageSnapshot.UsageCreditsBalance` (verbatim). `UsageSnapshot.IsZeroCreditBalance` (pure, unit-tested) is true only when the text has a digit and every digit is zero; `IsFableModelOffered()` reads it from the cached `LastUsageJson`. Fail-open on purpose: no snapshot, no section, no amount, or a snapshot cached by an older version (field absent) all keep Fable offered. Consumers: the 🤖 model menu (`ModelContextMenu_Opened`), both native-chat composer model menus, and the Recommend AI Model dialog picker — each still shows Fable when it is the current pick so the selection has a row; the dialog maps an advisor answer of `fable` to Opus with a note (the advisor schema itself is unchanged).

- Returning to the usage view after a manual account switch (v158.0): `TryRedirectToUsage`'s post-auth landing whitelist (`/new`, `/chats`, `/chat/`, `/projects`, `/recents`) deliberately excluded the root path, because `/` doubles as the signed-out home page and redirecting it unconditionally loops `/settings/usage → / → /settings/usage`. claude.ai drops a fresh sign-in on `/` about as often as on `/new`, so Switch Account → native "Log out" → sign in as a different user left the panel parked on the home page until the user pressed Refresh. `_sawSignedOutPage` (set whenever the embedded page visits `/login`, `/logout`, `/magic-link` or `/auth`) now promotes `/` to a landing, and `RedirectToUsageIfSettledAsync` requires a non-empty claude.ai `sessionKey` cookie (`HasClaudeSessionCookieAsync`) before navigating — a genuinely signed-out root reads no cookie and is left alone. The flag is cleared as the redirect fires, so a navigate that bounces straight back to `/` cannot re-arm it: one attempt per sign-out. The settle path re-checks `core.Source` both before and after the awaited cookie read, since the await gives the page another chance to move. `/onboarding` is deliberately *not* a landing — an account claude.ai forces through onboarding would ping-pong `/onboarding → /settings/usage` every ~6.5 s (1.5 s settle + 5 s debounce).

- Trim restore after Switch Account (`TryRestoreTrim`, v158.0): `SwitchAccountButton_Click` sets `window.__claudeSuppressTrim` so claude.ai's own chrome — and with it the account menu — stays visible. That flag lives on the document, so a full page load clears it by itself, but an SPA route change back to `/settings/usage` does not, leaving the raw settings page (sidebar and all) in the panel. Both `OnNavigationCompleted` and `OnSourceChanged` now clear the flag whenever the source is on `/settings/usage`, ahead of the redirect check.

-- Following a Claude CLI account switch (v221.0): the bars come from the WebView2's own claude.ai session, which has nothing to do with the CLI's credentials, so `/logout` + `/login` typed into the terminal (or `claude auth login` anywhere) moved the agent to another account while the bars kept scraping, and refreshing, the old one. Only the ⚙ "Change Account" items signed the page out. `SyncUsageWithClaudeAccountAsync` runs on every background tick (ahead of the foreground-tab guard) and once before the startup refresh. It reads `oauthAccount` from the active side's `~/.claude.json` (the distro's copy for `ClaudeCodeWSL`, with the `wslpath` result cached per session). `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is honored on both sides (`GetClaudeJsonPath`, `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME}` under WSL), because the CLI then keeps the file in that folder and never writes the one in the home directory. It identifies the account as `accountUuid/organizationUuid`, so switching organizations under the same login counts as a switch too, since usage limits are per organization. It falls back to the e-mail address when the UUIDs are missing. No `oauthAccount` (between `/logout` and `/login`) or a half-written file reads as "unknown" and never as a switch. The account the page was last paired with is kept per side (`windows`/`wsl`) in `usage-account.json` next to the settings, not in the settings. Every VS window saves its whole in-memory settings on each scrape, so a second window would write the old account back and then sign the shared page out a second time. The first check on a side only records the account. A window can find the pairing already moved to the account it now reads, because another window handled the switch. It then only drops its own cached snapshot (`_usageAccountSeen`), since its bars would otherwise sit on the old numbers until the next successful scrape. A change calls `SignOutUsageWindowIfActiveAsync(pairedAccount)`, which clears the cached snapshot, signs the page out and shows a main-window info bar (`InfoBarSlot.UsageAccount`) with an "Open Claude Usage" link. It deliberately does not pop the tab, which could steal focus while the user types. The Change Account menu items pass no account, which forgets the pairing, so the CLI login that follows is adopted silently instead of being handled as a second switch.

+- Following a Claude CLI account switch (v221.0, automatic sign-out removed in v310.0): v221 compared the CLI's `oauthAccount` (`~/.claude.json`, per side) with a pairing in `usage-account.json` and signed the usage page out on any difference. In practice it kept throwing away fresh Google sign-ins on the page (users had to sign in ~3 times), so v310 removed the pairing, `IsClaudeAccountSwitch` and the sign-out. `RefreshClaudeCliAccountAsync` (startup, background tick, composer usage refresh) now only re-reads the CLI e-mail for the composer usage popup (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` still honored via `GetClaudeJsonPath`; WSL path cached). The page is signed out only by the ⚙ Change Account items (`SignOutUsageWindowIfActiveAsync`, which also shows the `InfoBarSlot.UsageAccount` info bar) and by the page's own Sign Out / Switch Account buttons. The bars may therefore show the page's account rather than the CLI's after a CLI-only `/login` to another account.

- `SignOutAsync` used to delete cookies only on a live instance. When none was alive (never built this session, torn down with its hidden tab by #131, or a timed-out build), only `shared_cookies.json` went away. The `sessionKey` stayed in the persistent profile, and the next rebuild came straight back as the old account. It now builds an instance first (`_clearProfileOnNextBuild` makes `InitializeWebViewAsync` clear the profile before `LoadSharedCookiesAsync` and the first navigation). It clears with `Profile.ClearBrowsingDataAsync(AllSite)` rather than claude.ai cookies alone, because a "Continue with Google" sign-in keeps its own session in the profile and would silently sign the old account back in. It then navigates to the usage URL, and it resets the cookie-save throttle so the new account's first scrape writes `shared_cookies.json` immediately. `SignOutUsageWindowIfActiveAsync` gets the control through `GetUsageControlAsync`, which creates the hidden tool window when this session has not yet done so.

- Corporate proxy interstitial handling (`TryHandleUrlBlock`): Detects when `core.Source` ends with `/urlblock.php` (iboss/Forcepoint/Zscaler style block pages) and injects a JS poller that retries up to 25× at 200ms looking for the Continue submit button — multiple selector fallbacks (`input[type=submit][name=ok]` → generic `input[type=submit]` → `button[type=submit]` → `button[name=ok]` → `form.submit()`). Works while the tool window is hidden because CoreWebView2 processes navigation and JS without a visible rendering surface. Throttled to one click per 3 s. Triggered from both `OnNavigationCompleted` and `OnSourceChanged`

- Scrollbox preservation (v73.0): `isolatePath()` used to mark *every* ancestor between the isolation target and `<body>` as `data-claude-usage-path`, whose CSS forces `display:block; height:auto; overflow:visible` — this silently deleted claude.ai's own internal scroll pane (a `flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-y-auto` wrapper around the settings content), so anything below the initial fold (e.g. the Usage Credits spend/balance/buy-credits rows) was unreachable with no scrollbar at all. Fix: while walking up, the first ancestor whose *native* computed `overflow-y` is `auto`/`scroll` (checked before any of our own attributes could affect it) is tagged `data-claude-usage-scrollbox` instead of `-path`; every further ancestor above it is tagged the same way (`pastScrollbox` flag) since they're all part of its flex height-bounding chain. The `scrollbox` CSS rule only strips width caps/grid columns — it never touches `display`/`height`/`overflow`, so the pane's native scrollbar keeps working exactly as it does in a real browser tab.

content.text:
Tirei o logout automático da tela do Claude Usage. A mudança vai na versão 310.0, ainda sem commit. O build passou e os 1099 testes também, mas não testei no VS (F5), então ainda não sei se o login com o Google agora fica salvo.

**O que era o logout automático:** desde a v221 a extensão comparava a conta do Claude CLI com uma conta guardada da última vez. Se achasse diferença, deslogava a página de Usage e mostrava o aviso "Claude account changed…". Essa checagem rodava ao abrir o VS, a cada atualização em segundo plano das barras e ao atualizar o uso no chat. Se ela estiver vendo uma "troca de conta" que não aconteceu, isso explica ter que logar umas 3 vezes.

**O que mudou:**
- A checagem agora só lê o e-mail da conta do CLI, que aparece em "Account:" no popup de uso do chat. Ela não desloga mais nada.
- O resto dessa lógica foi apagado: a função que detectava a troca e o arquivo `usage-account.json` onde a conta ficava guardada (isso fica em `Controls/ClaudeCodeControl.Usage.cs`).
- O logout continua só quando você pede: no **Change Account** do menu ⚙ e nos botões **Sign Out** e **Switch Account** da própria página.
- Removi os testes da lógica apagada e coloquei um que garante que a checagem não desloga mais a página.
- Atualizei a versão, a entrada no README e a seção em `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

**Efeito colateral:** se você trocar de conta só no CLI (`/logout` + `/login` no terminal), as barras continuam mostrando a conta logada na página até você usar Switch Account.

Se o login com o Google ainda não ficar salvo, a causa não era esse logout automático. O próximo lugar a olhar é a cópia de cookies compartilhada entre janelas do VS. Deixei isso anotado na memória.

Quer que eu faça o commit?

content.content:
287:- Bar role: `meter` (was `progressbar`) + language-independent parsing (v54.0): Claude.ai's usage page switched the bars from `[role=progressbar]` to `[role=meter]` (inside `data-cds=Meter`) and localizes all labels ("Sessão atual"/"Todos os modelos"/"Fable"). The scraper had queried `[role=progressbar][aria-valuenow]` everywhere, so it found zero bars → `extract()` returned null (inline bars kept showing the stale cached snapshot) and page isolation found no target (full settings page with sidebar rendered instead of the trimmed block). Fixed by matching both roles via the `BAR_SEL`/`BAR_ROLE_SEL`/`isBarRole()` helpers (kept dual so a revert or cached page still parses) across `findSection`, `findIsolationTarget`, `clearStaleInlineWidths` (must skip meter descendants too, or it wipes the inline fill `width:63%`), the trim CSS, and `extract`. Row identification is now language-independent: labels read via `aria-labelledby`→`getElementById` (`readBarLabelAndReset`) with the `.text-primary` column as fallback, session/weekly matched by multi-language keyword regex but ultimately by document order (session = first bar; weekly = the aggregate "all models" bar, which always precedes per-model bars like Fable — so weekly falls back to "first row after session", never a per-model bar). `readUsedPercent` prefers `aria-valuetext` ("63% usado"/"63% used") so extra-usage percent survives localization and the >100% case. The old `div[tabindex=-1].outline-none` isolation target is gone from the page; the bar→`closest('section')`→`parentElement` (`div.pb-8`) fallback now supplies it. Pure JS fix — `UsageSnapshot` field names and the C# side are unchanged
290:- Returning to the usage view after a manual account switch (v158.0): `TryRedirectToUsage`'s post-auth landing whitelist (`/new`, `/chats`, `/chat/`, `/projects`, `/recents`) deliberately excluded the root path, because `/` doubles as the signed-out home page and redirecting it unconditionally loops `/settings/usage → / → /settings/usage`. claude.ai drops a fresh sign-in on `/` about as often as on `/new`, so Switch Account → native "Log out" → sign in as a different user left the panel parked on the home page until the user pressed Refresh. `_sawSignedOutPage` (set whenever the embedded page visits `/login`, `/logout`, `/magic-link` or `/auth`) now promotes `/` to a landing, and `RedirectToUsageIfSettledAsync` requires a non-empty claude.ai `sessionKey` cookie (`HasClaudeSessionCookieAsync`) before navigating — a genuinely signed-out root reads no cookie and is left alone. The flag is cleared as the redirect fires, so a navigate that bounces straight back to `/` cannot re-arm it: one attempt per sign-out. The settle path re-checks `core.Source` both before and after the awaited cookie read, since the await gives the page another chance to move. `/onboarding` is deliberately *not* a landing — an account claude.ai forces through onboarding would ping-pong `/onboarding → /settings/usage` every ~6.5 s (1.5 s settle + 5 s debounce).
291:- Trim restore after Switch Account (`TryRestoreTrim`, v158.0): `SwitchAccountButton_Click` sets `window.__claudeSuppressTrim` so claude.ai's own chrome — and with it the account menu — stays visible. That flag lives on the document, so a full page load clears it by itself, but an SPA route change back to `/settings/usage` does not, leaving the raw settings page (sidebar and all) in the panel. Both `OnNavigationCompleted` and `OnSourceChanged` now clear the flag whenever the source is on `/settings/usage`, ahead of the redirect check.
292:- Following a Claude CLI account switch (v221.0, automatic sign-out removed in v310.0): v221 compared the CLI's `oauthAccount` (`~/.claude.json`, per side) with a pairing in `usage-account.json` and signed the usage page out on any difference. In practice it kept throwing away fresh Google sign-ins on the page (users had to sign in ~3 times), so v310 removed the pairing, `IsClaudeAccountSwitch` and the sign-out. `RefreshClaudeCliAccountAsync` (startup, background tick, composer usage refresh) now only re-reads the CLI e-mail for the composer usage popup (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` still honored via `GetClaudeJsonPath`; WSL path cached). The page is signed out only by the ⚙ Change Account items (`SignOutUsageWindowIfActiveAsync`, which also shows the `InfoBarSlot.UsageAccount` info bar) and by the page's own Sign Out / Switch Account buttons. The bars may therefore show the page's account rather than the CLI's after a CLI-only `/login` to another account.

lines: - Follow-up — the `keep` rule was the same bug (v73.0): the ancestor-side fix alone didn't restore scrolling, because `findIsolationTarget()` can resolve to a `tabindex=-1` dialog shell (not just the small `div.pb-8` block) when the page has one — that shell itself commonly uses `display:flex; flex-direction:column` to stack a header above the internally-scrolling body. The `[data-claude-usage-keep="1"]` rule was still forcing `display:block !important` on the target, which collapses that flex-column and strips the scrollable child's bounded height (its `flex-1`/`min-h-0` become no-ops once the parent isn't a flex container) — the shell's own untouched `overflow:hidden` then just clips the excess with no scrollbar, no matter what the ancestor-side fix does. `keep` now only widens the target (`width`/`max-width`/`margin`/`box-sizing`) and leaves `display`/`height`/`overflow`/`padding` completely alone, same principle as the `scrollbox` rule.

- Docked tab painting over its neighbour (v230.0): the WebView2 is a native child window, so WPF clipping and z-order never apply to it. Measured on a tab docked in the document well with the Output pane below: the control's bottom edge landed at the bottom of the Output pane, i.e. it was laid out ~280 px taller than the area the shell shows, so the shell clipped the WPF elements (status bar) while the native window kept painting over Output. `ClaudeUsageControl`'s guard (`#region WebView2 bounds guard`) runs 150 ms after `SizeChanged`/`IsVisibleChanged`/the frame's `OnSize`, and on a 2 s heartbeat while the control is loaded. (1) `ClampWebViewToVisibleArea` hit-tests the `WebArea` grid (it has a `Transparent` background on purpose — WPF hit testing skips an element with no brush) down its middle: WPF hit testing honors the shell's clip, so the first point that no longer hits one of this control's own visuals is where the pane ends (one hit test when nothing is cut off, a ~7-step binary search otherwise). The web view host then gets an explicit `Height` of the visible part with `VerticalAlignment=Top` (not `MaxHeight`: a non-stretched host sizes to its content and an `HwndHost` desires 0); the clamp is released when the area is fully visible again. (2) `RepairWebViewBounds` compares `GetWindowRect(WebView.Handle)` with where WPF put the element (`PointToScreen` + `ActualWidth/Height` × the DPI transform) through the pure `HostedWindowBounds.IsMisaligned` (2 px tolerance, an element with no area never counts); a mismatch must be seen on two consecutive checks before anything is done, then `NudgeWebViewLayout` (width −1 px and back), and if the window is still wrong `SnapWindowTo` (`SetWindowPos`). Three failed repairs in a row back it off for 60 s. The off-screen scraper is skipped. Diagnostics: every change of state is appended to `%LocalAppData%\ClaudeCodeExtension\usage-layout.log` (control/area size, visible height, the frame's own `GetFramePos`, and — only while clipped — the ancestor chain with each element's vertical extent and clip flags; restarted past 200 KB). The popup has two halves: the context window of the chat's last completed turn (`ClaudeStatusLineInput` captured in `CompleteNativeTurn`/`CompleteNativeTurnForSession` into `_mainStatusLine` or `NativeChatSessionState.LastStatusLine`, cleared by Clear Chat), and the plan limits read from the cached `LastUsageJson` (the same numbers as the inline bars, so `NoWeeklyLimit`/`HasExtraUsage` are honored). The ring fills with context %, or with the session limit before any turn has reported a window. `HandleScrapedSnapshot` calls `RefreshChatUsageIndicators()`, so an open popup updates in place. Opening the popup raises `UsageRequested`, handled by `RefreshUsageForIndicatorAsync`: the same account-switch guard the background timer uses first, then `Reload()` when the tab is visible, otherwise `EnsureUsageToolWindowAsync(showWindow:false, updateWindowState:false, activate:false)`, so the tab never appears from a ring click. "See detailed breakdown" (`UsageDetailsRequested`) calls `EnsureUsageToolWindowAsync(showWindow:true)`, the same as the inline bars. The popup's "Updated / Not updated since" line uses `IsUsageSnapshotStale`. Formatting and ring geometry are pure (`ChatUsageIndicator`, unit-tested in `Tests/ChatUsageIndicatorTests.cs`). Popup rows (v236.0): label column `Auto`, value column `*` right-aligned with `CharacterEllipsis`; the border is `MinWidth=280`/`MaxWidth=440` instead of a fixed 280, because a long value ("0% used · Starts with your first message") in the old `*`/`Auto` layout squeezed the label column and drew over "Current session". `UsageNoPlanText` keeps `MaxWidth=256` so its wrapping does not stretch the popup. "Refreshing…" (v236.0): a ring click sets the view's `_usageRefreshing`, so the last line reads "Refreshing…" (snapshot pushes in the meantime only update the stored `_usageUpdatedText`) until the control calls `EndUsageRefresh()` on the clicked transcript when `RefreshUsageForIndicatorAsync` finishes. That task waits for real data: the off-screen path through `RefreshUsageInBackgroundAsync`'s own wait, the visible-tab `Reload()` path on `_indicatorScrapeTcs` (completed in `HandleScrapedSnapshot`, 15 s cap). A click while one is running joins the running `_indicatorRefresh` instead of starting another. Not F5-verified. The popup's wait is capped at `UsageRefreshTextCapMs` (20 s, v268.0): the off-screen path can chain a 10 s silent reload, a WebView2 rebuild (up to 30 s) and another 10 s wait, so "Refreshing…" could sit there over a minute after a fresh sign-in; the refresh itself keeps running and a later snapshot still updates the popup in place. Refresh ring (v276.0): the last line no longer swaps to "Refreshing…" (which hid the time); `UsageUpdatedRow` keeps the "Updated" text and shows `UsageRefreshSpinner` (10 px ring, tooltip "Refreshing…") beside it while `_usageRefreshing`. The rotation is started/stopped with `BeginAnimation` in `ShowUsageUpdatedText` only when the state flips, never by a style trigger (the v265.0 crash). Account line (v300.0, source changed in v301.0): the e-mail is the Claude CLI's own account, not the usage page's claude.ai login (the two can differ). `GetClaudeCliAccountIdAsync` (run by every `SyncUsageWithClaudeAccountAsync`: startup, background refresh, ring click) reads `.claude.json` once and also stores `oauthAccount.emailAddress` (`ParseClaudeAccountEmail`) per side (`windows`/`wsl`) in `_claudeCliAccountEmails`, re-pushing the indicators when it changes; `BuildChatUsageIndicatorData` takes it from `GetClaudeCliAccountEmail(provider)`, whether or not a snapshot exists. `UsageSnapshot.AccountEmail` (from the injected script's `/api/account` fetch) is still recorded but no longer shown and `UsageAccountText` at the bottom of the popup shows "Account: {0}" (collapsed when empty, e.g. a snapshot cached by an older version). `RefreshLanguage` redoes it.

- Icon-font glyphs in reset text (v268.0): claude.ai renders some icons as Private Use Area characters, and on some rows (seen on the Italian weekly row) the only `.text-secondary` element of the label column holds such an icon instead of a reset date, so `readLabelAndReset` took `U+E027` as `WeeklyReset` and VS drew it as a box. The scraper now strips `U+E000–U+F8FF` before choosing the reset text; `ChatUsageIndicator.StripIconGlyphs` does the same on the C# side (popup rows via `PlanRowText`, inline reset labels) so snapshots cached before the fix render clean too.
